title: Boss: the log ingest worker
summary: A real ticket: parse access logs in a hot path, count server errors without allocating, and let users run their own patterns without letting them take the service down.

steps.title: INGEST-77
body: > **INGEST-77: ingest worker: parse access logs in-process.** The Python prototype is too slow. Port it to
> the .NET worker. It handles 40,000 lines a second, and the dashboard lets users type their own search
Lines look like this: client IP, method, path, status, duration.
1. Write the line pattern (it will run with `NonBacktracking` in the prototype's test suite).
2. Count server errors (5xx) in a block of lines without allocating per match.
3. Parse a line into path, status and duration with a generated regex and a timeout.
4. Run a user's pattern safely: no crash, no hang, whatever they type.

steps.title: The line pattern
prompt: Match a whole access-log line with named groups `ip`, `method`, `path`, `status` and `ms`:
- `ip`: four groups of 1 to 3 ASCII digits separated by dots
- `method`: capital letters
- `path`: starts with `/`, no spaces
- `status`: three digits, `100` to `599`
- `ms`: ASCII digits followed by the literal `ms`
Single spaces separate the fields. The step runs with `NonBacktracking`, so no lookarounds or backreferences.

steps.title: Count the server errors
prompt: Write `int CountServerErrors(string log)`: how many lines of `log` (separated by `\n`) have a 5xx status.
Use `Regex.Count` with a pattern anchored per line, so no `Match` objects are created.
Careful: a 2xx line that took `500ms`, or a path like `/reports/500`, is **not** a server error. The status is
the field just before the duration. `System.Text.RegularExpressions` is already imported.
template: Dojo.Eq("a 500ms duration is not a 5xx", 0, CountServerErrors("10.0.0.9 GET /slow 200 500ms"));
Dojo.Eq("/reports/500 is a path, not a status", 0, CountServerErrors("10.0.0.9 GET /reports/500 200 12ms"));

steps.title: Parse a line
prompt: Write `static partial class AccessLog` with `public static (string Path, int Status, int Ms)? Parse(string line)`.
- Use a source-generated regex for the whole line (the pattern from the first step, anchored with `^` and `\z`).
- Add `RegexOptions.ExplicitCapture`: only the named groups capture, so the engine does less work.
- Lines come from outside, so give it `matchTimeoutMilliseconds: 100` and return `null` on
`RegexMatchTimeoutException`, exactly as for a line that does not match.
`Parse("10.0.0.7 GET /api/orders?id=4 200 35ms")` returns `("/api/orders?id=4", 200, 35)`.
`System.Text.RegularExpressions` is already imported.
starter: public static (string Path, int Status, int Ms)? Parse(string line)
solution: public static (string Path, int Status, int Ms)? Parse(string line)
template: Dojo.Eq("a GET line", ((string Path, int Status, int Ms)?)("/api/orders?id=4", 200, 35), AccessLog.Parse("10.0.0.7 GET /api/orders?id=4 200 35ms"));
Dojo.Eq("a slow 503", ((string Path, int Status, int Ms)?)("/api/pay", 503, 1204), AccessLog.Parse("192.168.1.20 POST /api/pay 503 1204ms"));
Dojo.Check("status 600 is rejected", AccessLog.Parse("10.0.0.7 GET /x 600 3ms") is null, "expected null");
Dojo.Check("garbage is rejected", AccessLog.Parse("garbage") is null, "expected null");
Dojo.Check("a trailing newline is rejected", AccessLog.Parse("10.0.0.7 GET /x 200 3ms\n") is null, "expected null: end with \\z");

steps.title: Run the user's pattern safely
prompt: The dashboard lets users type a pattern and shows how many matches it has. Write
`int CountMatches(string text, string userPattern)` that returns the count, or **-1** when the pattern
cannot be run safely. Whatever the user types, it must neither crash nor hang the worker:
- Build the regex with `RegexOptions.NonBacktracking` (linear time on any input) and a 200 ms timeout.
- An invalid pattern such as `(` throws `RegexParseException`, which is an `ArgumentException`.
- Lookarounds and backreferences throw `NotSupportedException` under `NonBacktracking`.
- Catch `RegexMatchTimeoutException` too.
`System.Text.RegularExpressions` is already imported.
solution: var regex = new Regex(userPattern, RegexOptions.NonBacktracking | RegexOptions.CultureInvariant, TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(200));
template: Dojo.Eq("a catastrophic pattern answers quickly", 0, CountMatches(new string('a', 5000) + "!", @"^(a+)+$"));

require.message: Handles constructs NonBacktracking does not support
